I can't give you that list, because both the client store (Toil & Trouble Home Products) and the firm store are empty. They contain no records of earlier matters, so there are no internal systems, document identifiers, or code names for me to report. Anything I listed would be invented, and a made-up list could lead you to misidentify documents when the production arrives.

Here is what I'd suggest instead:

1. **Check other sources for prior-matter records.** Possible sources include closed-matter files, prior productions and privilege logs, ESI protocols or custodian/data-source questionnaires from earlier matters, and any e-discovery vendor's processing reports.
2. **Ask the client directly.** Request an IT systems map or data-source inventory covering ERP, document management, email, chat, product-lifecycle or quality systems, and shared drives. Also ask for any known project code names, product line names, and internal naming conventions.
3. **Ask for Bates and control-number conventions.** Ask whether Toil & Trouble uses prefixes, document ID formats, or custodian codes, and whether these differ from what the vendor will apply.
4. **Look for identifiers when the production arrives.** Metadata fields such as file paths, system-generated IDs, email headers, footers, and templates often reveal internal systems and naming schemes. I can help build a running glossary as you review.

If you can share any earlier-matter materials or send me the client's answers, I can compile a reference list for B-2 from them.
